rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says esef can mean either intense anger or grief, depending on whether the disliked event comes from an inferior or superior; for Moses it denotes anger toward his people and grief before God.
rows.anchor: hem de hüzün mânasına gelir. Ve yerine göre her birinde kullanılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines esef as a state caused by something displeasing: when it comes from above it produces grief and constriction, and when from below it produces anger and agitation.
rows.anchor: o mekruh mâfevkten gelirse hüzün ve inkıbaz, mâdûndan gelirse gazab ve heyecan olur.

rows.speaker: Ebu’d-Derdâ
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda and many exegetes prefer the sense of intense anger, since the passage centers on Moses’ anger.
rows.anchor: evvelki Ebu’d-Derdâ radıyallâhu anh’ın kavli ve birçok müfessirînin muhtârıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı favors the intense-anger reading in context, rendering the phrase as Moses returning angry and extremely angry.
rows.anchor: Yani غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًۭا kızarak ve son derece kızarak demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On his return from the meeting, Moses had learned from God that his people had adopted the calf, so he returned in intense anger.
rows.anchor: kavminin ıcl ittihaz ettiklerini min tarafillah haber almış ve bundan dolayı gazab ü şiddetle dönmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebukes them for breaking his covenant and worshipping the calf after seeing his monotheistic worship and hearing his response to their earlier request for a god like others; their deputies also failed to stop the wrong.
rows.anchor: benim ahdime riayet etmeyerek arkamdan ne fena şeyler yaptınız ve buzağıya taptınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke also holds those left in charge responsible, since successors should honor their predecessor’s covenant and prevent such wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: makāmıma kāim olup böyle münkerâtı men‘etmesi lâzım gelenleriniz de bunu men‘etmediniz ha!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reading of Moses’ question is that the people hurried to abandon their religion and God’s promises.
rows.anchor: Yani dinini ve vaadlerini acele edip bırakıverdiniz mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed reading is that they impatiently expected the promised forty-night meeting to end, treating Moses as dead after thirty days and hastening to change their religion as other communities did after prophets.
rows.anchor: otuz gün geçer geçmez beni öldü farz ettiniz de peygamberlerinden bir zaman sonra birçok ümmetlerin dinlerini bozması âdet olduğu gibi siz de alelacele dininizi değiştirmeye mi kalktınız?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that they were rushing toward their Lord’s wrath and punishment.
rows.anchor: Veyahut alelacele Rabbinizin kahr u gazabını mı istediniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the tablets broke when Moses cast them down: six-sevenths were taken away and one remained, containing guidance and mercy while the removed portion contained detailed explanation of everything.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki bırakılınca elvâh kırılmış ve binâen‘aleyh yedide altısı ref‘olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that the Qur’an contains no statement that the tablets broke in this way.
rows.anchor: lâkin Kur’an’da elvâhın böyle kırıldığını ifade eder bir kayıt görünmüyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He instead understands Moses to have temporarily set aside the tablets, which contained detailed guidance and mercy, so he could first address the crisis in the foundation of religion: monotheism.
rows.anchor: esas meseleyi şiddetle halletmek için tafsîlâta ait olan ve hüdâ ve rahmeti mutazammın bulunan elvâhı muvakkaten bir tarafa bırakmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode depicts something like declaring emergency rule in response to a grave upheaval threatening the foundation of monotheism.
rows.anchor: Bunda esâs-ı tevhîde ta‘alluk eden büyük bir ihtilâl karşısında idâre-i örfiye ilânına misâl veren bir hâdise tasvîri var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By seizing Harun first, Moses shows that religious duty takes precedence even over regard for his brother.
rows.anchor: Din işinde evvelâ kardeş hatırına bile bakmıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Moses had appointed Harun as his successor, he begins by holding him responsible.
rows.anchor: Kardeşini yerine halef bırakmış olduğundan evvelemirde onun mes’ûliyetinden başlıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ first action also shows that working together with his brother for monotheism was the priority.
rows.anchor: Kardeş ile tevhîd-i mesâî etmek ilk iş olduğunu gösteriyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun calls Moses “son of my mother” despite their being full brothers to awaken his tenderness: their mother signifies mercy, especially for Moses, and was a believer.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Hârûn Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın şakīki, ana baba bir biraderi olduğu hâlde böyle hitap etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harun says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him, then asks Moses not to give their enemies cause to gloat or count him among the unjust; he disowns their actions and says he did not deserve blame for failing to stop them.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh düşmanları benimle şemâtet ettirme, yani bana düşmanları sevindirecek bir şey yapma.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line says death is lighter than the enemies’ gloating, using shamatat for their malicious rejoicing.
rows.anchor: وَالْمَوْتُ دُونَ شَمَاتَةِ الأَْعْدَاءِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks forgiveness for himself first, conceding that his treatment of Harun did not arise from any established sin by Harun and thereby apologizing and showing affection before those who might gloat.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ kendisi için istiğfârı, biraderine yaptığı muâmele onun sâbit olmuş bir günahından nâşî olmadığını itiraf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses also asks forgiveness for Harun because Harun had delayed fighting the unjust group although Elmalılı says it was obligatory for him to fight them.
rows.anchor: biraderi için istiğfârı da o gürûh-ı zâlimîn ile mukātele etmesi vâcib olduğu hâlde tehir etmiş olduğundan dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request goes beyond forgiveness, asking that both brothers be placed within God’s abundant favor and mercy.
rows.anchor: Mağfiretten başka bizi rahmetinin, ziyade in‘âmının içinde bulundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Most Merciful grounds strong hope that they will remain within the sphere of mercy in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: kaviyyen ümit ederiz ki dünya ve âhiret dâire-i rahmetinde bulunuruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf adopters meant here are Samiri and his followers, who made the calf, initiated the disturbance, followed it, and persisted; the next verse separately treats those who repent.
rows.anchor: yani Sâmirî ve tarafdârânı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The persistent calf worshippers will meet an indescribably severe divine anger in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: istikbalde bunlara bir gazab, tasvîre sığmaz uhrevî bir gazab-ı rabbânî erecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly abasement became proverbial across the world and extended to them and their descendants.
rows.anchor: Bu, o gariplik zilletidir ki bütün âleme darb-ı mesel olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samiri also received the specific humiliation of being forbidden social contact, as the account in Ta-Ha later explains.
rows.anchor: ibtilâsı ile nâsa ihtilâttan memnû‘iyettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning applies to all who invent religion against God: they ultimately face anger and humiliation, so it is not confined to Israelite calf makers.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bunu yalnız Benî İsrâil ıclcilerine münhasır zannetmemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who commit any kind of evil but then sincerely repent, believe, stop persisting, and act in accordance with faith can know that their Lord is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: seyyiât yapanlar herhangi seyyie olursa olsun yapıp da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı presents the forgiveness promise as the answer to the earlier plea that, without the Lord’s mercy and forgiveness, they would be among the losers.
rows.anchor: diyenlerin cevâbı da bunun içindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that anger fell silent means that Moses’ anger became calm and disappeared.
rows.anchor: Vaktâ ki Mûsâ’dan gazab, sükût etti yani sükûnet buldu, zâil oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is a vivid metaphor: anger acts like a powerful commander urging Moses to speak harshly, set aside the tablets, and pull Harun by the head, then falls silent after Harun’s mild and sincere appeal.
rows.anchor: Gazab, Mûsâ üzerinde mütehakkim bir âmire benziyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once his anger subsided, Moses took up the tablets he had set down.
rows.anchor: bıraktığı elvâhı eline aldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writing on the tablets contained guidance and mercy, directing people toward good and right conduct, but it was specifically for those who fear disobeying God for His sake.
rows.anchor: Hayr u salâha irşâd ile bir nimet vardı fakat herkese değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage then turns to their beginning repentance.
rows.anchor: Bunun üzerine şu suretle tevbeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses selected seventy of the best people for the appointed time, bringing them for repentance.
rows.anchor: En hayırlıları olmak üzere yetmiş kişi intihab eyledi de tâyin ettiğimiz vakt-i mahsusta tevbe için aldı getirdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify this meeting with the earlier meeting to receive speech, but Elmalılı infers from the Qur’an’s separation of the stories and some reports that it was another meeting for repentance after the calf episode.
rows.anchor: bundan evvel geçen mîkāt-ı kelâm diyenler olmuşsa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says it is possible that the earlier meeting comprised thirty nights and this one added ten after Moses returned, completing forty; he says this reading, which Abu Muslim held, reconciles the other reports.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kāil olduğu bu surette diğer rivayetlerin bir telifi var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God directed selected Israelites to come repent of calf worship and ask for acceptance of the remaining people’s repentance, appointing a time for this.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya Benî İsrâil’den müntehab birtakım kimselerin gelip ıcle ta‘abbüdden i‘tizâr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the report, Moses chose six men from each of the twelve tribes, then asked two to stay when the number exceeded seventy; after they disagreed, Caleb and Joshua stayed while Moses went with the other seventy.
rows.anchor: On iki sıbtın her birinden altı kişi seçmiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses ordered the group to fast and purify themselves and their clothes before setting out for Sinai.
rows.anchor: oruç tutmalarını, tetahhur ve elbiselerini tathir eylemelerini emretti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As they approached the mountain, fog enveloped them; Moses entered it with them, they prostrated, and they heard God command Moses, including the order that they kill themselves in repentance.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ Mûsâ’ya dilediği gibi emr ü nehy ediyor, onlar da işitiyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says they may have refused to believe until seeing God because they doubted Moses’ report that God had ordered self-killing, found the command too difficult, and conditioned belief on sight by analogy with hearing speech.
rows.anchor: “biz Allah’ı açıktan açığa görmedikçe sana kat‘iyyen inanmayız” dediler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shaking is explained, by reference to al-Baqara, as either a thunderbolt or an earthquake that made them faint, and perhaps die.
rows.anchor: yıldırım çarptı veya dağda bir zelzele ile yıkılıp bayıldılar ve belki öldüler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says God could have destroyed them earlier for failing to forbid calf worship, neglecting their duties, and not separating from those who persisted; God had also been able to destroy Moses when he had asked to see Him.
rows.anchor: buzağıya tapmaktan nehiyde kusur ettikleri, gereği gibi vazifelerini yapmadıkları ve ona tapanların ısrarlarını gördükleri hâlde onlardan ayrılmadıkları sırada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By recalling that God spared them earlier, Moses seeks pardon for what is happening now: they had deserved destruction, but God had chosen not to destroy them then.
rows.anchor: Bu söz afv-ı sâbıkı beyan ile afv-ı lâhıkı isticlâb demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks God not to destroy everyone for the foolish people’s act; fools are light-minded people who do not understand wisdom or restrain themselves at moments of danger.
rows.anchor: hikmetini bilmez, kayacak noktalarda kendini tutamaz hafif akıllıların

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls the episode God’s trial and says the sinners are excused insofar as it came from God: hearing the divine speech overwhelmed them, and they followed a false analogy while grasping for what lay beyond them.
rows.anchor: Bu süfehânın düştükleri fitne, sırf senden gelen bir mihnet ü ibtilâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through this trial God leads astray those who cannot hold themselves steady and guides those whose faith grows stronger and who remain firm in comparable situations.
rows.anchor: İmanı kuvvet bulur da emsâlinde sarsılmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God their sole guardian means He alone rules, helps, and protects their worldly and otherworldly affairs.
rows.anchor: Sen bizim yegane velîmizsin: Dünyevî, uhrevî umûrumuzda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses pleads for forgiveness and mercy, and calls God the best forgiver because His forgiveness is the finest and is given without self-interest or compensation.
rows.anchor: garazsız ivazsız en güzel mağfireti Sen yaparsın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea for a good worldly life asks for safety, well-being, and a life fit for good deeds, free of hardship and evil, including release from the demand that they kill themselves.
rows.anchor: şiddetten, meşakkatten, fenalıktan ârî, önü sonu temiz bir hayat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the afterlife, Moses asks that their final outcome be Paradise, complete deliverance, and happiness.
rows.anchor: de cennet ve mahz-ı felâh u saadet olması vâcib

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says they have turned back to God and invoke the promise in 7:153 that repentance is followed by forgiveness and mercy; he asks God to accept the delegation and return them forgiven and shown mercy.
rows.anchor: çünkü biz Sana döndük, tevbe ettik yani Sen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses presents this supplication, apology, plea for forgiveness, and repentance to God on behalf of the group after the shaking.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ, Rabbine böyle isti‘tâf u i‘tizâr ve istiğfâr u istirham ile dua ve tevbelerini arz eyledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment reaches whomever He wills, while His mercy encompasses every kind of thing in this world, including believers, unbelievers, accountable and unaccountable beings, and all future things.
rows.anchor: Dünyada mü’min kâfir, mükellef gayr-i mükellef, hatta “şey” unvânı dâhilinde her ne varsa hepsini kaplamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every thing has shared in the Merciful’s mercy from its first existence; even Iblis once dwelt in gardens and was granted a period in response to his request.
rows.anchor: recâsı bir müddete kadar is‘âf olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal mercy does not mean equal shares or that everyone remains under mercy forever; God may punish whomever He wills, and His punishment is just, either containing mercy for them or fitting people who have made themselves undeserving of compassion.
rows.anchor: Fakat bunun böyle olması her şeyin hisse-i rahmette müsâvî olmasını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine mercy is universal and primary, but it does not bind God to continue showing mercy to everyone; His will may bring punishment to anyone.
rows.anchor: rahmet-i ilâhiye umûmî ve her şeye vâsi‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from future tense for punishment to past tense for encompassing mercy shows that mercy’s scope is primordial, while punishment pertains to a later stage; mercy is fundamental and punishment arises from people’s circumstances.
rows.anchor: şümûl-i rahmet mebde’, meşiyyet-i azab da vasat veya müntehâ itibariyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since punishment is conditioned by God’s will, mercy too is limited prospectively by His will: it belongs to those for whom He wills it.
rows.anchor: Madem ki kimi dilerse azab ile musâb edebilecektir, o hâlde rahmeti de kimi dilerse onadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between punishment reaching whom God wills and mercy having encompassed every thing limits mercy’s universality in the future: those chosen for punishment leave the scope of mercy they had previously shared.
rows.anchor: İstikbalde ta‘zîbine meşiyyet ta‘alluk edenler mâzîde rahmetin mütenâveli olan كُلَّ شَيْء’de dâhil iken çıkarılıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ request for good in both lives and for mercy to be made binding seeks to remove the possibility of punishment; God first rejects the demand that mercy be obligatory, then partly grants the request while stirring hope in mercy.
rows.anchor: taleb-i vücûb ibtidâen redd-i beliğ ile reddedilmiş ve ba‘dehû kısmen kabul ile buyurulmuştur ki:
